entities.name: Big Beanie
entities.description:
Big Beanie is a large Chilli Pepper-like Beanie residing on Egg Island in Yoshi's New Island, he started out as a normal-sized Beanie before being enlarged into a giant Beanstalk-like creature by Kamek. He is the boss of World 1 and the game's first major boss. Big Beanie is fought in the Clouds high above his castle. Defeating Big Beanie will unlock World 2.

After Blue Yoshi and Baby Mario survive Big Beanie's Castle and reach the large room, a small Beanie will descend from the ceiling and Kamek will appear and taunt Yoshi before using his Magic Hammer to make the Beanie grow into a massive Beanstalk. Yoshi can climb the Beanstalk out of the Castle and into the clouds where he finds the Beanie at the top has grown into Big Beanie.

Big Beanie starts the battle by dangling from his Beanstalk, Yoshi can hit the Big Beanie in the head with an egg, Big Beanie will then get angry and a prickly vine will temporarily shield him from any more attacks, during this time, prickly vines will emerge from the cloudy ground periodically to attack Yoshi, these vines can be annoying to avoid but keep an eye on the ground below to gauge where they will emerge, Big Beanie will then replace the prickly vines with a normal vine, during this time, Big Beanie will spit Beanies at Yoshi (these are more of a help than a hindrance as the Beanies work as an egg supply if Yoshi is running low on eggs), hit the vine with an egg, this will leave Big Beanie exposed, hit him again with an egg, following the second hit, he will shield himself again with a thorny vine and several more will periodically emerge from the cloudy floor below Yoshi which he must avoid (or he may lose Stars thereby making it tricky to get 100 Points). When the attack is done, Big Beanie will bring back the regular vine and resume spitting out his Beanie underlinings, hit the vine with an egg again to leave Big Beanie exposed then hit Big Beanie once more to finish him off and complete the World.

entities.name: Big Blob
entities.description:
Big Blob is a mini-boss in Virtual Boy Wario Land.

Wario fights the Big Blob in Stage 7. At one point, the Big Blob is found asleep, blocking a door which leads further into the level. None of Wario's attacks are effective against the Big Blob, so if he tries to attack it, Big Blob only briefly opens its eyes before going back to sleep.

To defeat the Big Blob, Wario has to break several nearby blocks so that a Torny can enter the area. When the Torny touches the Big Blob, the Big Blob quickly shrinks, showing a sad face, and is defeated. Because of this, the door leading to the next area is revealed.

entities.name: Big Blooper
entities.description:
Big Blooper is a boss who appears in Chapter 3-2 of Super Paper Mario.

The Big Blooper is a Blooper who gigantic enough to occupy even most of the background space. It has several tentacles with only one having red suction cups on it while the rest are blue.

As Mario, Princess Peach, and Bowser swim through the Tile Pool in order to reach Fort Francis to rescue Tippi, the Big Blooper suddenly appears upset that there are trespassers. It is blocking the way to the Tile Pool, therefore preventing the party from reaching Fort Francis. Big Blooper traps off the heroes and engages them in battle. After the heroes defeat the Big Blooper, it swims away never be seen again.

During the battle against Big Blooper, the player may damage it by jumping on the tentacles when they are sticking up out of the water. The player may also use Thudley to ground-pound the tentacles or use Bowser's Fire Breath to damage them. If the player miss a tentacle when ground pounding, they will lose Heart Points. Slamming or burning the blue tentacles makes the more-sensitive red tentacles bob upward with more frequency. If Mario goes into 3D and tries to leave, the Big Blooper's tentacles will block the way.
entities.short_description: Big Blooper is a boss who appears in Chapter 3-2 of Super Paper Mario.

entities.name: Big Bullet Bill
entities.description:
Big Bullet Bill is a Bullet Bill similar in size to a Banzai Bill. Even though they are a larger variety of a Mario enemy, Big Bullet Bills have only appeared in the of crossover games.

Big Bullet Bill appears as a rival boss and is similar in size to a Banzai Bill. The player meets him in Skeleton (Single Festival), Bobsleigh (Team Festival), and Blazing Bobsleigh (DS Adventure Mode).

Big Bullet Bill is first faced in the Skeleton Bobsleigh event in Festival mode. Since he can fly, he has no need for a bobsled and he can maneuver through the course with ease. If the player loses, Big Bullet Bill will fly proudly towards the sky, soon after Cream proclaims that the match was not fair because Big Bullet Bill could fly. If the player is the winner, Big Bullet Bill will fly away slowly towards and behind the crowd.

In the Adventure Tours mode of the Nintendo DS version, he appears at the end of Cubyrinth, where he keeps Icy in a cage, and will only release the Snow Spirit if the player defeats him in Blazing Bobsleigh.

entities.name: Big Bungee Piranha
entities.description:
Big Bungee Piranha is huge Piranha Plant and the castle boss of World 2 in Yoshi's Island DS. It is a Bungee Piranha enlarged by Kamek. Like all Bungee Piranhas, it hangs from the ceiling and lunges down to bite Blue Yoshi, though unlike others it is accompanied by smaller, harmful Bungee Buds, which follow Big Bungee Piranha's lunges or move on their own. To beat him, Yoshi must stand on top of a Chomp Rock, and when Big Bungee Piranha reaches down to devour him, Yoshi must move out of the way quickly, and Big Bungee Piranha will bite down on the Chomp Rock and howl in pain for a few seconds, revealing his weak spot; his tongue. After two hits, Big Bungee Piranha becomes progressively faster. After the third hit, the massive creature will be decimated and fall at Yoshi's feet.

In Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, Big Bungee Piranha is mentioned briefly by Viridi during Palutena's Guidance dialogue for Piranha Plant.

entities.name: Big Buzzy Beetle
entities.description:
The Big Buzzy Beetle is giant-sized Buzzy Beetle who appears as a mini-boss in Paper Mario: Sticker Star. It resides in the caves beneath Hither Thither Hill.

The Big Buzzy Beetle is basically a giant version of smaller Buzzy Beetles.

Mario fights the Big Buzzy Beetle just as he is about to leave the mines of Hither Thither Hill. Mario must use the Battle Spinner technique in order to do some damage on the Big Buzzy Beetle since it always flips itself over right on the next turn. POW Blocks and Jump stickers are helpful in this fight. After the Big Buzzy Beetle is defeated, the way is cleared and Mario is awarded with a HP-Up Heart.

Being a large Buzzy Beetle, the Big Buzzy Beetle is very durable and is able to withstand any attack. Like any Buzzy Beetle, the Big Buzzy Beetle's weak point is it's soft underside belly but the Big Buzzy Beetle is also pretty agile and is able to get back up the moment it is flipped, to flip it over, use the Battle Spinner and get at least two matching slots (the best way to ensure this is to use the Special and Slow options which ensure you get at least two), from here, use a Jump sticker or a POW Block to flip it over (or alternatively, getting three POW Blocks on the Battle Spinner will also flip it over), then use a Jump based Sticker such as the Shiny Jump to whale on it. Make sure you use your more powerful stickers second or third because these are crucial to bringing down the Big Buzzy Beetle. Alternatively, the use of any Things you may have obtained earlier such as the Scissors or the Faucet are extremely effective as not only do they do heaps of damage but they will ignore the Big Buzzy Beetle's defensive measures and do normal damage without having to flip him over. Combining two or more Things together will also allow Mario to get a Perfect Bonus which comes with a huge Coin reward.

entities.name: Big Cheep Cheep
entities.description:
Big Cheep-Cheep is a mini-boss in Paper Mario: Sticker Star. it is fought in Surfshine Harbor and is much bigger than a regular Cheep Cheep and even a Mega Cheep Cheep.

Before the Blue Toad and Mario could leave Surfshine Harbor on the boat, the Big-Cheep Cheep intercepts them by blocking the ship's path and rocking the boat with it's great force. Mario exits his boat and goes on the docks to engage the Big Cheep-Cheep in battle. In battle, the Big Cheep-Cheep mainly attacks by jumping into Mario, dealing 3 damage. After the Big Cheep-Cheep has taken a certain amount of damage (the HP amount doesn't go anywhere below 20 HP at this point to prevent the second phase from being skippable), it will swim into the ocean water in the background and begin to heal itself fully and uses a new attack that sprays water at Mario, which deals 10 damage and may make Mario Soggy. Mario must use the Fishhook thing to bring the behemoth back onto land otherwise any of his other attacks won't be able to reach the colossal fish. Afterwards, the Big Cheep-Cheep will grow even bigger, doubling his attack on the second turn, and again on the third. Mario must take down the Big Cheep-Cheep in five turns or it will explode, dealing 99 unblockable damage and usually defeating Mario. Additionally, Mario can quickly end the fight by using either a Spike Helmet sticker or the Thumbtack thing sticker to pop the Big Cheep-Cheep but must be careful as he will take a large amount damage in recoil, based on how big he is. Alternatively, Mario can use the Sponge or similar thing sticker to block the devastating explosion. The Big Cheep Cheep can easily be beaten with Hopslippers as well as Flashy and Big Shiny Stickers, additionally, Things can also be used to deal huge damage to the Big Cheep-Cheep. After the Big Cheep-Cheep is defeated, Mario can sail onto the last three Worlds.

Big Cheep Cheeps appears in Water-themed stages, usually as a more powerful form of normal Cheep Cheeps. They have a fairly high amount of health, and deal decent damage. They can use "Bash" to deal even higher damage, or at half health can use "Healing" to restore 50% health to the entire enemy team. Their main attribute is Water and their sub-attribute is Light. They have high health and recovery stats, but low attack, and their skill is Healing, which restores 2,000 HP and turns Wood Orbs into Heart Orbs. They require Comet Medals to skill up, and can be acquired either by evolving a Cheep Cheep by using 4 Ice Flowers, or have a low chance to be dropped by a Cheep Chomp. They can also evolve into a Cheep Chomp for 6 Ice Flowers. After the 2.0 update, they gained the basic awakening of Water Boost, increasing Water attribute damage for the team when matching a full row of Water Orbs.

entities.name: Big Daddy of Blooper-surfing
entities.description:
The Big Daddy of Blooper-surfing or Big Daddy for short (also known as Big Daddy Blooper-surfer, Blooper-surfing Big Daddy, or simply Bloopy) is a character in Super Mario Sunshine.

He is a tan-colored Pianta who wears a straw hat and a light-green shirt.

He is the very friendly owner of the green, pink, and yellow Blooper Racers in Ricco Harbor, allowing Mario to ride them for free, although he "waives all liability for accidents," as crashing a Blooper instantly makes Mario lose a life.

The Big Daddy of Blooper-surfing appears in two episodes of Ricco Harbor, both of which involve Mario riding a Blooper Racer. He first appears in Episode 2: Blooper Surfing Safari, where Mario has to ride on a Blooper Racer during a timed race. If Mario clears the race fast enough, the Big Daddy of Blooper-surfing gives him a Shine Sprite. If Mario does not, he loses an extra life from failing to meet the object. Next, in Episode 6: Red Coins on the Water, the Big Daddy of Blooper-surfing leases Mario a Blooper Racer for free, as Mario is required to ride one to collect all of the Red Coins within the time limit.

Big Guy the Stilted is a giant robotic Shy Guy on Stilts operated by multiple Shy Guys in Yoshi's Island DS. He is the fourth main boss of the game, and is fought inside his castle, where he resides alongside many Shy Guys. To defeat him, Blue Yoshi must use eggs (or Baby Bowser's fire breath) to knock Big Guy the Stilted off the edge of the platform they are fighting on, which is surrounded by lava, giving Blue Yoshi a chance to ground-pound him. Many Shy Guys are inside this robot, jumping out occasionally, making for an easy egg supply. After three Ground Pounds, it cracks, exposing all of the Shy Guy operators, after which it falls into the lava.

entities.name: Big Lantern Ghost
entities.description:
The Big Lantern Ghost is the mid-boss of Shy Guy's Toy Box from Paper Mario. He is a giant Lantern Ghost with a bandage on his forehead who resides in a dark room. After being defeated in battle, Mario learns that the Big Lantern Ghost had been holding Watt prisoner inside of his lantern.

At the start of the battle, the Big Lantern Ghost cannot be attacked directly. In order to target him, the player must repeatedly attack the lantern that he holds in order to spread light through the room and render him visible for attack. Once the lantern's light is large enough, he will occasionally blow into the lantern to extinguish it and become unavailable to target again. The Big Lantern Ghost is also capable of casting a ring of light from his lantern, dealing two damage to Mario and incapacitating his partner for several turns unless guarded against. Once the player defeats him, he flees and drops his lantern, which Watt is trapped in. After freeing her by breaking the lantern, Watt joins Mario's party as his sixth partner.

entities.name: Big Massif
entities.description:
Big Massif is a character and boss that appears in Mario & Luigi: Dream Team. He is the older brother of Lil' Massif and is the founder of the Beef-Off. There is an X Boss called Big Massif X.

Big Massif is a large, brown Hooski that wears a red shirt with a black belt. He has a dark brown angry unibrow. He also has a mustache, to resemble Mario. His appearance resembles his brother, Lil' Massif.

Both Massif brothers speak with a slight russian accent.

Mario, Luigi, Starlow, and Prince Dreambert all need a tour guide up the mountain and Lil' Massif says that his older brother Big Massif is the only one who can do it. Mario and Luigi eventually find Big Massif sleeping on a Dreampoint where it was revealed that he can get tougher training in the dream world. Luigi then sleeps beside Big Massif while Mario enters into Luigi's dreams to find Big Massif. Mario and Dreamy Luigi then walk around in Dreamy Wakeport until they run into the tour guide receptionist. He tells Mario and Dreamy Luigi that they must complete the Beef-Off first and they do so. It was then revealed that the receptionist was Big Massif himself all along and challenges Mario and Dreamy Luigi to a fight. He ends up losing and realizes that he can get stronger in the real world and leaves out of his dreams. After, he and his brother take Mario & Luigi to Mt. Pajamaja and help them get to the summit.

entities.name: Big Pokey
entities.description:
Big Pokey is a large Pokey found in Mario & Luigi: Paper Jam. He is seen residing in Doop Doop Dunes alongside the Tower Power Pokey near the bridge leading to Bowser's Castle ready to knock down anyone who dares to cross the bridge.

Big Pokey is the boss of Doop Doop Dunes alongside Tower Power Pokey. Big Pokey started out as a Giant Pokey living in Doop Doop Dunes. After Luigi accidentally opened the Paper Mario Book unleashing the paper world on the regular world, the Tower Power Pokey landed near the Big Pokey and from there, the two of them guarded the bridge to Bowser's Castle knocking over anybody who tries to cross it (sending them down to Doop Doop Dunes Grotto). Mario, Luigi, and Paper Mario made a couple attempts to cross the bridge during their time at the desert but failed thanks to the colossal Pokey duo falling down to Doop Doop Dunes Grotto each time.

As the heroes are traversing the Doop Doop Dunes Grotto, they later find the towering Pokeys and use their Hammers to knock away the Pokeys' segments, Big Pokey and Tower Power Pokey aren't to happy about this so they engage the heroes in battle. The Pokeys put up a good fight but the heroes are too powerful and best the Pokeys, after their defeat, Big Pokey and Giant Pokey lose all their segments and their heads explode. This allows the heroes to traverse across the bridge unhindered form this point forward.

In battle, the Big Pokey has a few attacks which can cause some devastating blows to the heroes. His first attack involves him lying on the ground and attempting to roll at Mario, Luigi, and Paper Mario which they must jump over. If they are hit by this attack, they can be Tripped so avoid it at all costs, the plumbers can also take damage by landing on the Big Pokey due to his segments being spiked. The Big Pokey can also toss his segments at the plumbers which they must knock back with their Hammers, the third attack involves the Big Pokey and Paper Tower Power Pokey chasing the plumbers down the arena and attempting to dart at them. If one of the Pokeys is darting, they must use the paper airplane folded-Paper Mario to glide above, if the plumbers are hit by the rampaging Pokeys, they will suffer heavy damage however if the chase goes on for long enough, the two Pokeys will tire out before tripping allowing Paper Mario to stomp on them both. If one Pokey has more segments than the other, both Pokeys will eventually regenerate all their lost segments.

Big the Cat is a character from the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise. He made his first overall appearance in Sonic Adventure, but Big's first Mario-related appearance is in the Wii version of Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Games.

Big the Cat appears as a referee for the Athletics and Rowing events. He can also be seen behind the podium in the Athletics events during the awards ceremony.

Big the Cat appears as a VIP Member, and along with Birdo is the only character to give the player a costume as well as 100 Star Points. There is also an unlockable Mii costume of Big the Cat.

Big plays a role in Adventure Tours, where he can be found in Polastraits. Here, Big wonders what is the "sign" near him. Amy tries to explain to Big that each mission's details is written there, although because Big does not understand. When Amy completes Big's mission, taking place in Alpine Skiing GS, he understands what Amy was trying to tell him, and rewards the party with a Spark Luge.

entities.description:
Big Top is MC Ballyhoo's hat who serves as his cohost in Mario Party 8. He also holds all of the coins for Chump Charity, stating that he was glad to get the load off his head. Big Top not only has the ability of speech but is also his own separate entity. In Super Smash Bros. Brawl, he shares a trophy with Ballyhoo. Big Top's name comes from a phrase referring to large circus tents. The "Top" part of his name is also a reference to the fact that he is a top hat. His appearance bears a resemblance to the Bonneter, but he is not confirmed to be a member of the species.

Big Top is a dark-blue top hat with a strip of light blue close to the rim. He has a small mouth and two differently colored eyes: one teal, one pink. His eyes have rather big eyelashes.

Big Top and MC Ballyhoo appear as a Novice class spirit in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

Billdit is a character in Mario & Luigi: Brothership.

Billdit is a yellow skinned humanoid based off of a electrical outlet, Billdit wears a red aprin that looks like a design of a Hammer and has a white headband with a red "leaf" coming out of his head. He has patches on his low right hand face

A woman named Willma decided to have two kids, their names where Billdit and Maykit. Willma is a hard worker and is very determined to do everything she can. But when she gets older she cant do all the hard work she could do before. So, she did everything she could and taught Billdit and Maykit how to be just like her. Billdit loves the idea and goes out on adventures.

After meeting Willma, she starts to get worried about her kids because of the separation with the islands and is wondering if you could go find them. Before you find one of her kids you first have to pick which one you want to run the shop at Shipshape Island. If you chose Billdit, you will head to Raynforst Island. Once there you will meet Billdit who is suspicious of the Bros. after some puzzle solving and linking the Island, Billdit will come onto Shipshape Island and joins your adventure. After that he starts making equipment for you sucks as Hammers, Gloves, and Accessories to help you in combat.

Bink is a sailor that appears in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga and its Nintendo 3DS remake, Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga + Bowser's Minions. Mario and Luigi have to complete his Barrel minigame to get a Membership Card to gain access to the bunker of the S.S. Chuckola, where a sailor that holds a piece of the Beanstar is at. Mario and Luigi cannot replay this minigame until they get to the Little Fungitown arcade, where Bink also reappears. In the mandatory play of Bink's Barrel minigame, Mario and Luigi must match five barrels in a row ten times to win.

In the original game, Bink resembles a skeletal Kong, particularly Donkey Kong. He also throws the barrels onto the board in his minigame, which is a reference to Donkey Kong, and eats bananas when he is bored. In the 3DS remake, Bink uses the same character model as the rest of the sailors, a drastic change to his appearance compared to the original version.

entities.name: Birdo
entities.description:
Birdo, also self-referred to as Birdetta and once by the shorthand Birdie, is a recurring character in the Mario franchise. She is a prehistoric dinosaur, identified in some early sources as a bird, with a funnel-shaped mouth from which she can spit eggs. Her first appearance was as an enemy in Yume Kōjō: Doki Doki Panic, which was rebranded as Super Mario Bros. 2. She is considered one of the first video game characters.

Since her first appearance, Birdo appeared in various spin-off series of the franchise, with her original role as an antagonist being ostensibly scrapped in favor of a newer role as a more neutral character. However, she continues to be occasionally classified as an enemy, as is the case with the Super Mario Trading Card Collection and her being grouped with typically antagonistic characters in the driver list of Mario Kart Tour. Some games portray her as a close friend or even significant other of Yoshi, while others show her simply allying with whoever catches her interest at that moment. Birdo has also been merchandised into figurines, plush toys, and amiibo cards.

While Birdo is often portrayed as an individual character, there have also been many appearances of multiple Birdos that come in different colors and that sometimes have different characteristics. In most cases, these are depicted with the same feminine characteristics as the main Birdo.

Birdo and the rest of her species are dinosaurs with funnel-shaped mouths and a body structure similar to a Yoshi, though slightly shorter and with a row of three spikes on the tail, not the head. In several early illustrations, she is depicted as being orange instead of pink, and on the cover of Yume Kōjō: Doki Doki Panic, she is depicted with distinct nostrils midway up her snout and what appears to be a tongue in her mouth, though neither of these traits has ever been shown again. In the various iterations of Super Mario Bros. 2, her snout ends with a small hole and is somewhat barrel-shaped, inverting while it is open; later games, however, use the latter shape in all situations, likely due to looking that way in her original artwork.

entities.name: Blablanadon
entities.description:
Blablanadon is a pterosaur-like creature who helps Mario and Luigi get to the top of Hoohoo Mountain (and near the end of the game, Bowser's Castle) in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga and its remake, Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga + Bowser's Minions. His name is a portmanteau of "blah blah blah", a phrase used to mock incessant talking, and "Pteranodon", the name for a type of pterosaur.

In the beginning, Blablanadon is absent from his nest in Hoohoo Village. The brothers have to hike up to the top of Hoohoo Mountain where they find him sleeping on a large egg he found next to a Hoohoo Block, which contains Dragohoho, who attacks the brothers after knocking Blablanadon away by spitting out a Hoohoo Block. After Dragohoho is defeated, he reverts to Prince Peasley, who was changed by Fawful's magic. After that point, Blablanadon can be found on his nest in Hoohoo Village, where he offers to fly the Mario Bros. to the top of Hoohoo Mountain at any time. After the Mario Bros.' quest in Joke's End, Bowletta attacks the Beanbean Kingdom from Bowser's Castle. Mario and Luigi have to find Blablanadon and hitch a ride on him to reach Bowser's Castle and back when they escape while Prince Peasley detonated the castle. Because he flies Mario and Luigi to Bowser's Castle, if they want to go to the top of Hoohoo Mountain after that point, they have to manually travel there.

entities.name: Black Bowser
entities.description:
Black Bowser (referred simply as Bowser in-game) is the black main villain in Paper Mario: Color Splash. He is one of Paper Bowser´s variants were the black paint absorbs and controlls him in which he becomes an ultimate evil vilian who´s main goal is to cover the power of the black paint over the entire world via mixing with every colour his Koopa Troops collect to add in his bomb factory.

When Bowser came to Port Prisma, he saw the Prisma Fountain with its rainbow of colors and decided he wanted a rainbow colored shell. Bowser jumped in and mixed all of the paint together while jumping around and created Black Paint, which proceeded to climb onto his body while he was trying to have fun. Then the Black Paint possessed him, and he became Black Bowser. He flings the Big Paint Stars far away and shortly afterwards, orders Slurp Guys to suck out the paint of almost everything there.

After Mario and Huey return the Red Big Paint Star to Port Prisma, Black Bowser appears on the highest spire of the Red District. He delivers an ominous message that the dark gift of black paint will be shared with the world soon. He then leaves Port Prisma by jumping onto an airship, which carries Princess Peach away to Black Bowser's Castle where she was later drained from her paintings and hanged as as an art. He later reappears in the memories given by the Big Paint Stars, telling how he became the monster he was.

After Mario and Huey destroy Black Bowser's Factory, they confront Black Bowser in the castle's throne room for a final standoff. During the battle, Black Bowser unleashes a series of powerful attacks, including a charged spin shell strike, fiery breath, and the summoning of Black Lava Bubbles from the remnants of black paint scattered across the ground. If Mario fails to eliminate these bubbles before his next turn, they dissolve back into Bowser, replenishing his black paint reserves.

entities.name: Black Cat
entities.description:
The Black Cat is a mysterious cat who appears in Wario Land 4 as both a guide and an ally to Wario.

The Black Cat first appears in the cutscene shown when booting up the game. She is almost hit by the Wario Car as Wario dashes his way to the Golden Pyramid when he heard about all of the treasure found within. The Black Cat gets to the Golden Pyramid before Wario and guides him to the main area.

During Wario's journey in the Golden Pyramid, the Black Cat makes some appearances, such as from entering an Item Shop in the corridor preceding a boss fight. The Black Cat has the ability to transform into other forms, namely the shop owner.

When Wario reaches the Golden Diva, the Black Cat tries to attack the Golden Diva, but is unsuccessful. The Golden Diva sucks the Black Cat into her nose, starting Wario's battle against the Golden Diva. When the Golden Diva's lips are attacked, the Black Cat emerges and guides Wario out of the Golden Pyramid before it gets destroyed. Once they have escaped, the Black Cat reveals herself to be Princess Shokora, who formerly ruled over the Golden Pyramid area.

entities.name: Black Chest Demon
entities.description:
"Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door (Nintendo Switch)" (2024)

The Black Chest Demons are the Four Heroes that sealed the Shadow Queen with the power of the Crystal Stars. The Black Chest Demons are seen in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door.

The Wise Goomba was one of the heroes that sealed away the Shadow Queen. She came from Boggly Woods where she used her knowledge to help get rid of all the monsters in Boggly Woods. When she and the other heroes were in dire situation, the Wise Goomba suggested using the Crystal Stars to damage the Shadow Queen. However, this doesn't work well and she suggested using the Crystal Stars to seal away the Shadow Queen. The Shadow Queen was sealed away but she used one last trick to curse all of the heroes. The Wise Goomba heads back to The Great Tree where she hid the Crystal Star in the tree. However, the Punis were being tormented by the monsters of Boggly Woods so the Wise Goomba hollowed out the tree so that the Punis can leave in safety. The Wise Goomba's soul was then sealed away.

The Stalwart Koopa was a Koopa that traveled the world alone. He noticed the darkness creeping and monsters soon fought him. The Stalwart Koopa was getting overwhelmed until a brave Boo saved him with her magic. Later, during the battle with the Shadow Queen, the Stalwart Koopa manages to damage her using the Crystal Stars. However, after going with the Wise Goomba's plan, he and the other Four Heroes manage to seal away the Shadow Queen. Unfortunately, the Stalwart Koopa and the rest were cursed just as the Shadow Queen was fully sealed up. The Stalwart Koopa then heads for a southern isle to hide the Crystal Star. However, the Stalwart Koopa was tired from his journey and Cortez, the Pirate King, stole the Crystal Star from the Stalwart Koopa causing his soul to be sealed away in a black chest.

entities.name: Black Jewel
entities.description:
The Black Jewel (written in lowercase as black jewel in Wario World and alternatively called the Evil Black Jewel in the game's Nintendo Power guide and official website) is the main antagonist and final boss in Wario World. Prior to the events of the game, Wario obliviously collected the evil Black Jewel, assuming it was simply another treasure, and it destroyed the newly-renovated Wario Castle once it awoke. Despite its name, it is actually purple (although its name may refer to its dark nature), and has one eye and several pink appendages somewhat resembling octopus arms.

According to Wario Worlds intro movie, the jewel once fed on peoples' wishes to grow power. It eventually grew so powerful, it became a huge threat to civilization, sending armies of evil spirits across the land in an attempt to conquer the world. The Spritelings were able to overpower and capture it somehow, and seal it away within their ruins. Many years later, long after these events were forgotten, Wario found the black jewel and stole it, unbeknownst to the dreadful powers it held.

On the night that Wario is celebrating his huge gains in his newly-built castle, the jewel re-awakens, destroys the castle, turns most of Wario's treasures into monsters, and scatters the rest. Wario falls and lands in what has become of his castle; a strange hub-world with four main worlds attached to it, known as Treasure Square. Wario must complete these worlds and defeat their bosses in order to acquire the Huge Treasure Chest Key that will open the black jewel's Treasure Chest.

As a boss, the black jewel has three attacks. The first one is using its eye to fire a laser and scorch the ground, creating a wall of fire. It will use this attack until Wario is trapped between two walls of fire narrow enough. If the space is very narrow, the black jewel will lower itself to the ground and fire shockwaves in each color of the rainbow across the floor which will have to be jumped over, similar to those that Bowser makes in the final battle of Super Mario 64. If the fire-walls are not very narrow, the black jewel will fire homing fireballs from its eye.

The Black Jibberjay is a Jibberjay and a character who appears in Super Mario Galaxy 2. He is the fastest of the Jibberjays as well as their leader. He races Mario on two separate occasions, and he and the other Jibberjays send Mario a letter, inviting him to do so beforehand each time.

The Black Jibberjay is first encountered in the Wild Glide Galaxy. He is raced during the mission Jungle Fluzzard Race, in which Mario has to ride Fluzzard to the finish line at the end before Black Jibberjay and the other Jibberjay contestants in order to win. When Mario wins, the Black Jibberjay rewards Mario with a Power Star as a trophy and declares him the new leader of the Jibberjays.

Mario races the Black Jibberjay a second time in the Fleet Glide Galaxy, during the mission Fastest Feathers in the Galaxy. Unlike last time, Mario only races the Black Jibberjay, not the other Jibberyjay racers. When Mario wins again, the Black Jibberjay gives him another Power Star.

entities.name: Black Mage
entities.description:
Black Mage is a job class from the Final Fantasy franchise. They are characterized by their distinctive appearance—blue robes and a face shrouded in shadow beneath their pointed hat—as well as their practice of Black Magic, which consists of various offensive, elemental spells. In the Mario franchise, Black Mage's design is a mix of his classic appearance from Final Fantasy as well as Black Waltz 3, a boss from Final Fantasy IX.

An individual representative character appears in Mario Hoops 3-on-3, a game developed by Square Enix, creators of the Final Fantasy series of games. He is one of several characters based on Final Fantasy, the others being Ninja, White Mage, Moogle, and Cactuar. He has a magical staff which he uses to perform his Special Shot. He is classified as a Tricky player, meaning he makes very swift moves to dodge tackles.

He is unlocked by winning a Gold Trophy in the Rainbow Tourney on the Normal difficulty. An alternate costume can also be unlocked by completing the Rainbow Tourney on the Hard difficulty. This alternate costume gives Black Mage a green and black color scheme.

Black Mage, along with the other Final Fantasy characters return in the Wii follow-up, Mario Sports Mix. He is unlocked by clearing the hidden path in the Star Cup, Star Road, three times, winning the Star Cup four times, or by going on one of the two alternate paths during the Mushroom Cup replay and winning against Blue Toad. His best stat is technique, while his other stats are fairly low. Unlike other characters, in hockey, he uses his magical staff in place of a hockey stick. His stats are identical to those of Daisy and Waluigi.

entities.name: Black Paint Bowser
entities.description:
He looks like himself but has black paint covering all of his body and yellow eyes. The black paint is constantly dripping off his hands and shell like gooey black ooze, similar to the Goop from Super Mario Sunshine.

Bowser came to Port Prisma one day and spotted the Prisma Fountain. He thought of the idea of a rainbow-colored shell, so he jumped into the center of the Fountain and spun his shell around. But instead of getting rainbow paint, he mixed all the colors and created black paint. He was having fun until the black paint became sentient and started to consume him. Bowser tried to resist, but he gave in to the dark influence and merged with it, transforming into Black Paint Bowser. He had one goal in mind: to paint the entire world in black and envelop it in eternal despair. He equipped most of his Shy Guys with straws that could suck up paint from objects. He transported all that paint to his floating castle, mixed it into black paint in the factory, then filled Banzai Bills with the toxic substance. He might have also sent his Koopalings to collect the Big Paint Stars because he knew that they could supply him with all the paint he needed to make more black paint. His plan was stopped by Mario, who faced off with him in his castle at the end of the game. When he lost a substantial amount of black paint, he used all of his paint up in a last ditch effort. entities.description:
Blanka is a beast-like character hailing from Brazil from the Street Fighter series.

Blanka and several other characters from the Street Fighter II series appear in the Club Nintendo comic "Super Mario Klemp-Won-Do: Muskeln sind nicht alles!". He can be seen laughing along with the others when Mario decides to enter the "Street Fighter II grandmaster" tournament.

Mario faces Blanka as his third opponent; Toad arrives to assist Mario and gives him bananas. Mario cleverly spreads them across the ring's floor, causing Blanka to accidentally slip on one of the peels and fall right out of the boxing ring, disqualifying him and allowing Mario to advance.

Blanka appears in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate as a spirit, using his artwork from Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers. The Blanka spirit battle being against a green Donkey Kong with a Screw Attack equipped references Blanka's beastly nature, as well as his electric-based attacks in the Street Fighter series.

Blappy is an old Blobule (72 years old to be exact) that is purple in color.

During the events of Chapter 4-2, Blappy can be found in his house at the very end of Planet Blobule. He is known as the elder of Planet Blobule and mentions that he was searching for a certain treasure in space. However, his direct role is to sell the Ancient Clue to the heroes for 1,000 coins. However, this is an amount that the heroes cannot possibly hold (as the maximum coin amount held is 999) and must refuse this offer where Blappy can drop it to 100 coins. They can also decline his offer and Blappy will drop the price to 10 coins. The heroes must accept this offer, or Blappy will bring the price back up to 100 coins and will not drop the price again.

entities.description:
Blathers is a character from the Animal Crossing series, in which he is the museum curator. He has made a few cameo appearances in the Super Smash Bros. series as well as the Mario franchise and its spinoffs.

Blathers is a dark brown-feathered owl who wears a green bowtie. His face is light-colored and consists of large, white eyes with black pupils, a yellow beak, large, feathered eyebrows, and round, pink cheeks. Blathers' eyebrows are lined with light-brown dots. Being an owl, Blathers has a pair of wings for arms and a pair of yellow talons for legs. A curved, white line is near the tip of both of Blathers' wings. There are three light brown stripes on Blathers' legs and pointed, white toenails. Blathers' chest has a distinct white and light brown-checkered pattern.

Blathers has a phobia of bugs, which is mentioned in his various trophy descriptions. As an owl, Blathers is always found sleeping during the daytime.

Blathers has only made cameo appearances within the Super Smash Bros. series.

Blaze was originally withdrawn and aloof until she met Cream the Rabbit, whom she learned the meaning and value of friendship from, along with Sonic and Tails.

entities.description:
Blinky is a red ghost from the Pac-Man franchise. He is the leader of the other ghosts, Inky, Pinky, and Clyde, and together they oppose Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man. Blinky debuted in the same game as Pac-Man, simply titled Pac-Man. He has made some crossovers with Mario characters.

Blinky makes his Super Mario franchise debut in Mario Kart Arcade GP, where he, alongside Pac-Man and Ms. Pac-Man, appears as a playable character due to the game being developed by Bandai Namco Holdings. Blinky's special items are Monster Shield, Monster's Hammer, Petit Monster, Flare Ball, and Ghost Morph. His emblem is a sprite of himself from the Pac-Man arcade game. Blinky's arcade sprite also appears in the Pac Labyrinth course.

Blinky returns as a playable character in Mario Kart Arcade GP 2. In this game, when in his standard kart, he has exceptional acceleration, but poor weight and top speed, sharing these statistics with Peach and Yoshi. In his personal kart, Blinky has great acceleration, but poor weight and average top speed.

Although Blinky is no longer playable in Mario Kart Arcade GP DX, a sprite of him appears on the Pac-Man Stadium course, and he appears at the start of the Pac-Man Cup, along with the other ghosts, using their designs from the original Pac-Man arcade game.

Blizza is one of the snow spirits featured in the Adventure Tours mode of Mario & Sonic at the Olympic Winter Games for the Nintendo DS.

Blizza has the appearance of a large, levitating purple snowflake with black eyes.

Blizza is the snow spirit of Blizland. It is the sixth and final snow spirit found by both Mario and Sonic at Icepeak, when they meet up with Rouge, Dr. Eggman, and Bowser at the end. The two villains bribe Rogue with several Whitestones, and Dr. Eggman even strikes a deal that if Mario and Sonic's team wins against her in Figure Skating, he will release Blizza, whom he vaguely refers to as a snow spirit at first.

Even when the player's character wins against Rogue, Dr. Eggman and Bowser get frustrated and reluctantly free Blizza, who properly introduces himself to both Mario and Sonic. Releasing Blizza was a trick set up by both Dr. Eggman and Bowser, as they then decide to capture Frosty. Blizza joins the heroes, and they continue onward to Blizland. Here, Blizza can melt an ice wall if Mario and Sonic's team have four crystals.

entities.name: Blizzard Midbus
entities.description:
Blizzard Midbus is the fifteenth boss in Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story and its remake Mario & Luigi: Bowser's Inside Story + Bowser Jr.'s Journey.

Blizzard Midbus is fought by Bowser. He has been powered up by Fawful's ray gun for his final battle, and has 2041 HP, (2580 HP in the 3DS remake) which is higher than the last four bosses in the game (five if counting Super Peach's Castle of Fury).

One of his new attacks is throwing snowballs at Bowser from the top screen. This is avoided by Bowser ducking. If (at least) three snowballs have been dodged, Blizzard Midbus will get mad and try to punch Bowser. This is countered by Bowser's own punch. Another one of his attacks involves him going off the battlefield and roll at Bowser in a giant snowball. Bowser has to punch the Bob-omb buried inside to counter it. Occasionally, Midbus will spawn four Snawfuls from his crown. The Snawfuls can attack Bowser by throwing snowballs at Bowser while Blizzard Midbus is crawling up a wall. Then he rolls up into a ball and flies at him. This is countered by Bowser punching or ducking. When inhaled by Bowser and left to Mario & Luigi, the Snawful's shovel position indicates which Bro they will hit (lifted up for Mario, kept down for Luigi). Snawfuls restore 30 HP to Blizzard Midbus if they aren't inhaled or defeated quickly. Each Snawful killed by Mario and Luigi fills up a meter. If the meter reaches (at least) five Snawfuls total, Bowser will spit out a cloud of snow that turns into ice and plugs up Blizard Midbus' crown, preventing him from spawning more Snawfuls. Snawfuls killed by Bowser won't fill up the meter. When Midbus loses a lot of health, the Bob-omb Snowball attack will not show the Bob-omb in the snowball. After his defeat, Blizzard Midbus will turn into a block of ice.

entities.name: Blizzaurus
entities.description:
Blizzaurus is an ice dragon and a boss who appears in Super Princess Peach. Her name is a portmanteau of "blizzard" and the suffix "-saurus". She is battled at the end of World 6, Gleam Glacier.

At first, Blizzaurus appears as a giant cyan dragon-type boss with a blue mane, but her true form is revealed to be a sprite-like creature. In her fairy form, Blizzaurus has light blue skin and wears a sleeveless dress and a golden headband with pink orbs on it. She carries a golden wand that lets her perform magic attacks.

When Princess Peach enters the boss room, she sees an imprisoned Toad (or a stash of Coins if she completed the level beforehand). Blizzaurus catches the princess off guard with her ice breath and then charges, breaking her free and beginning the fight proper.

During battle, Blizzaurus mainly attacks with her massive body by charging directly at Peach. She can also create glaciers from the ground. She has an ice beam that freezes anything touching it. Princess Peach can deal damage onto Blizzaurus' ice shield by using her Rage vibe. Successfully breaking Blizzaurus' ice shield causes her to lose a hit point; when this happens, Blizzaurus rears back in pain as she gains crosses for eyes.

entities.name: Bloat
entities.description:
Bloat is a sailor who appears in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga and its remake. His name comes from the word meaning "to become swollen with fluid," which is appropriate; after drinking excessive amounts of Chuckola Cola, he became incredibly obese and somehow managed to wedge himself stuck in a crack in the S.S. Chuckola. His crew mates refer to him as an "Ostaf" (which is "Fatso" backwards), and he hiccups and belches repeatedly in his dialogue.

Mario and Luigi are offered a Beanstar piece in exchange for freeing Bloat from the wall. Using dynamite, the duo blasts Bloat out from the crack, also ripping a hole in the ship that causes sand from Teehee Valley to pour in. The force of the sand pouring inside the ship pushes it into the sea, where it proceeds to crash into a rock, sinking the S.S. Chuckola into Oho Ocean.

entities.name: Blockafeller
entities.description:
Yoshi's Crafted World is a 2019 platform video game developed by Good-Feel and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo Switch. Serving as a spin-off of the Mario franchise and the spiritual successor to Yoshi's Woolly World (2015), it is the eighth main installment in the Yoshi series and the fourth released for a home console. The game was revealed at E3 2017 and was released worldwide on March 29, 2019.

Yoshi's Crafted World follows the Yoshis as they venture to collect the scattered gems of the Sundream Stone, which has the ability to grant wishes, before Kamek and Baby Bowser can.

The game received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its visuals, level design, and gameplay, though the soundtrack and lack of difficulty elicited criticism. Yoshi's Crafted World sold more than one million copies worldwide in three days and more than three million units by December 2022, making it one of the best-selling games on the Nintendo Switch. The game was succeeded by Yoshi and the Mysterious Book for the Nintendo Switch 2 in 2026.

entities.name: Blockhead Bowser
entities.description:
Blockhead Bowser is the form Bowser takes when he and the Mario Party crew face off in the minigame Bowser's Block Party in Mario Party DS. It serves as the final boss of the game.

Bowser becomes Blockhead Bowser when he puts on and activates his Megamorph Belt, turning him into a sentient square block cluster consisting of a golden Bowser block that serves as his weak spot and can shoot fire, blocks with Bowser's emblem that can shoot fire, and regular grey blocks that do nothing except form his body. Throughout the battle, Blockhead Bowser stacks the blocks forming his body into the forms of a top, a cube, and a worm-/snake-like form.

As with the other bosses in the game, Blockhead Bowser is fought in three phases, with his life bar being represented with three hearts, which each take five hits to deplete; thusly, he has a total of 15 hit points. The battle takes place in a circular stone arena surrounded by lava and a thunderbolt scrawled in the centre.

During the first phase of his battle, Blockhead Bowser transforms into a top that spins around, flinging fireballs. Eventually, the boss's body will light on fire before he gets dizzy and falls over. If his weak spot is close to the ground, Blockhead Bowser can be attacked just by punching his weak spot. Otherwise, the player has to jump up and kick it to deal damage. After five hits to his weak spot, Blockhead Bowser falls apart.

Blooey is a character that appears in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door. He is one of Luigi's partners that joins him on his separate journey for the Marvelous Compass. Originally known as the "White Torpedo," and Luigi went onto a journey to Rumblebump Volcano, but things went wrong and Blooey got into an accident, which ended up making his flesh golden brown and made him hold a grudge with Luigi.

Blooey is a brown Blooper. He was originally white prior to his accident. Luigi accidentally threw him into a volcano when they were battling a stone creature, turning Blooey into a golden brown color.

Blooey is shown to be full of anger after Luigi basically made him "edible." Blooey stated that the only reason why he is going with Luigi on his journey is to, one day, pay him back for burning him. He even states that he'll get back at Luigi even it takes him his entire life. However, at the end, he got thrown in lava again. This time, however, he decided not to hold a grudge against Luigi anymore due to Princess Eclair deciding to marry the Chestnut King which upsets Luigi and Blooey himself was quite pleased by Luigi's misfortune.

Blowfish is a character in Mario Party 3.

Blowfish is a giant anglerfish with an arrow at the end of its fin ray.

The Blowfish is found in the board Deep Bloober Sea. When a player lands on a Happening Space near the anglerfish, the arrow on its fin ray points to the bottom, front, or right of the board. The anglerfish then inhales all players in front of it like a vacuum. To avoid being sucked into Blowfish, players must press repeatedly to escape the suction. Players that fail are sucked into the anglerfish, then spat out in the direction the arrow fin points towards, landing them at the start, near a pink Sushi, or near a Boo.

Blue Mario refers to various unidentifiable counterparts of Mario who wear blue clothing. One such character first made a minor cameo in Mario Tennis. Just like Yellow Mario, it is unknown whether he is just a colored copy of Mario or if he is a relative. Both he and the mysterious Yellow Mario also appear in the 4-player mode of the Mario Bros. remake for the Game Boy Advance. He also appears as an alternate costume in all Super Smash Bros. games. it is unknown whether he is just a colored copy of Mario, or if he is a relative.

While he wears a blue cap and shirt in all his appearances, his other clothes have been different; in the Mario Bros. Remake, it is white, in Super Smash Bros., Super Smash Bros. Melee, and Super Smash Bros. Brawl it is red, in all subsequent Super Smash Bros. games, it is pink, and in Mario Tennis, he has a variety of different outfits.

"Blue Mario", as his "name" suggests, bears a strong resemblance to Mario, with most of Mario's red features being replaced by Blue. he also wears white overalls, howewer, in Mario Tennis he has many different referee outfits, with all of them including a red bowtie.

entities.name: Blue Toad
entities.description:
Blue Toad, also known as just Toad, is a Toad who made his first appearance in New Super Mario Bros. Wii as a playable sidekick for Mario, along with Luigi and Yellow Toad. Blue Toad and Yellow Toad reprise their roles as playable characters in New Super Mario Bros. U, and they have appeared in various other games as well.

Like many other Toads, Blue Toad is a short, mushroom-like creature. He has a white cap with blue spots. He wears a blue vest with gold lining, a pair of white dress pants, and a pair of brown shoes. He is about a head shorter than Mario, and is almost always seen smiling.

In New Super Mario Bros. Wii, Blue Toad is shown as a courageous character, who is able to venture alongside the Mario Bros. on their dangerous mission to save Princess Peach from Bowser and his minions; a force that most Toads tend to be afraid of. He is also shown to be kind and compassionate as seen in the ending of the game where he happily invites Luigi to ride in his and Yellow Toad's hot air balloon after he had been abandoned (albeit by accident) by Mario and Peach. In the introduction of New Super Mario Bros. U, Blue Toad is shown to be even more finicky than his partner Yellow Toad as he is seen to be in an extreme alarm when Bowser's mechanical arm pulled away the Princess.

Throughout the New Super Mario Bros. games, Blue Toad plays similarly to Mario. While possessing the same jumps as Mario, he is also shown to use similar techniques as well including the Wall Jump and Ground Pound. He is also able to maximize his jumps by using a Spin Jump. Unlike the Mario Bros. however, Blue Toad (along with Yellow Toad) are shown to have a unique triple jump; the two Toads perform a high jump similar to a cartwheel while facing one side of the screen. Blue Toad is also shown to be quite strong, being able to carry items much larger than his own size (such as barrels). He is also capable of picking up, carrying and throwing other characters (such as Mario) with ease. All of these traits are similar to not give players advantages over each other. In New Super Luigi U, Blue Toad has the ability to perform a scuttle jump much like Luigi.

Bluster Kong is a character from the Donkey Kong Country TV series. He runs Kongo Bongo Island's resident barrel factory, named Bluster Barrelworks although it is actually owned by his unseen mother. Occasionally, he speaks with his mother on a mobile phone. He is constantly hitting on Candy Kong, his lone employee, despite the fact that she is dating Donkey Kong. Bluster is depicted as a stereotypical rich, spoiled coward. It is unknown if his affluence was inspired by Swanky Kong, who is implied to be wealthy. He is the antagonist of several episodes, though he is more of a nuisance than a genuine threat such as King K. Rool

entities.name: Boards
entities.description:
Boards are a group of four ostensibly sentient Signposts that appear in Super Mario Galaxy. They are named Gil Board, Bill Board, Phil Board, and Jill Board respectively, and all of them teach Mario how to perform a certain move.

All four Boards have the same appearance as a regular wooden Signpost with a letter pinned to it. By extension, every Board has an identical appearance to one another. Jill Board is supposedly female, given her name, whereas the other three Boards all have a name generally given to males.

When talked to, every Board says "Hey!" before talking to Mario. Aside from being able to talk, Boards have little difference from regular Signposts. A few of them show up in multiple galaxies, namely Bill Board, but it is not shown whether they appear in several galaxies at once or travel between them accordingly. Given that several galaxies can be explored in a nonlinear order, galaxies with the same gimmick also feature the same Board, allowing Mario to learn about the gimmick regardless of which order he explores

Every Board has a name that is a pun of "billboard." They have a first name, followed by "Board." Bill Board is pronounced the same as billboard, but is still a pun because Bill is the first name.

entities.name: Bob-omb
entities.description:
In the live-action movie Super Mario Bros., a Bob-omb appears after Mario and Luigi escape the de-evolution chamber. As they are fleeing from Koopa's Goombas,

Luigi notices that some fungus appears to be offering them the explosive, but Mario drags him away before he can accept it. Later, after they leave the Boom Boom Bar, the fungus again offers them the Bob-omb. This time, Luigi manages to grab it before he and Mario escape.

Later, near the end of the film, while facing Koopa on the catwalk, Mario pulls out the Bob-omb, which causes mass amounts of panic amongst the city's inhabitants. Realizing the power the object possesses, he winds up the key and places it on the ground, but before it can get to Koopa, it falls through a crack in the ground. However, unbeknownst to both of them, the Bob-omb continues its journey after it falls. It walks through the lower section of the city (scaring off the inhabitants there), up a wall, and along the underside of the catwalk. As Mario and Luigi are blasting Koopa with Devolution Guns, the Bob-omb finally reaches Koopa and explodes right underneath him.

The appearance of the Bob-omb is similar to that in the games, though there are some differences. For instance, the wind-up key appears on the side rather than on its back, its eyes are smaller and more circular than their in-game appearances, and its feet have three toes on it. Additionally, the Bob-omb walks like a wind-up toy, and before the Bob-omb explodes from underneath Koopa, the Reebok brand name as well as the Union Jack (often used on their brand name products) can be seen on the underside of the feet.

Until the player returns to him, Bob-omb was curious if the player knew the password, Bob-omb was impressed and rewarded him the Gaddget.

entities.description:
Bobo is a giant bird and the guard of the Black Sugar Gang's pirate ship, the SS Tea Cup. He appears as the area's boss in both Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3 and Wario Land II.

Bobo is the fifth boss of Wario Land. In it, he attempts to hurt Wario by releasing Watches from his mouth or trying to trying blow him off into the pit on the side of the battlefield. To defeat him, Wario has to use the Watches to propel himself high enough to be able to jump on Bobo's head. It takes three jumps to defeat him. Alternatively, Wario can use the Dragon Pot power to blast Bobo's head or pick up fallen Watches and throw them at Bobo's head three times.

Bobo is the second boss of Wario Land II, where he is considerably smaller than in his original appearance. He only attacks Wario directly in this game by repeatedly swooping down and flying back up again in patterns that change as the battle progresses. Bobo is also able to make wind come up from the ground by flapping his wings, making Wario fly upwards and forcing him back to an earlier section of the boss level unless he crouches. He can be defeated by jumping on him six times or Ground Pounding him three times. Every two hits (or one hit with a Ground Pound), his attack pattern changes. First it is a large and slow curve, then it's in the shape of a w, and finally it is in three lines with 90 degree sharp turns. In addition, every attack pattern transition forces Wario to stay crouched longer.

Bobolink is a character who is mentioned in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door.

Bobolink is a female Bob-omb that was mentioned by Swob as he expressed his love for her. Swob even wrote a special message to Bobolink on the 50th floor of the Pit of 100 Trials asking to her to marry him. Swob did this because he heard that any wish will come true by writing a message on the 50th floor of the Pit of 100 Trials. Mario can accept this request and use Admiral Bobbery to remove the graffiti off of the wall.

entities.name: Boddle
entities.description:
Boddle is a Beanish character that appears in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga and its remake, Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga + Bowser's Minions. He is the curator of the Yoshi Theater and the younger brother of Bubbles. He is the founder and the president of the Yoshi Fan Club while considering himself to be the biggest Yoshi fan, and even wears a large Yoshi Egg-like costume.

After the Beanstar splits into four pieces during the events at Woohoo Hooniversity, Mario and Luigi are tasked with finding all the Beanstar pieces along with Prince Peasley. One of the Beanstar pieces lands in the Yoshi Theater. Boddle is first seen placing the Beanstar Piece on the theater's entrance sign.

When Mario and Luigi come to ask about the Beanstar piece, Boddle's assistant, Tuki, immediately marks them for swindlers and tries to shoo them off. As he then begs Boddle to ignore the Bros., Boddle responds by withdrawing into his costume (which pulls up a Yoshi's Island-style targeting cursor) and hitting Tuki for his impudence. As he apologizes for Tuki's rudeness, the Mario Bros. seem to recognize him and freak out, explaining to the confused Boddle that he looks like Bubbles. Boddle reveals that he is in fact Bubbles's younger brother, displaying a similarly eccentric tendency toward pirouetting, before introducing himself as the owner of the Yoshi Theater and founder/president of the Yoshi Fan Club.

When the Mario Bros. explain that they must have the Beanstar piece being used on the theater's sign, Boddle considers the matter for a few moments before agreeing to do so, with Tuki's protests causing Boddle to hit him again. He then proposes a trade for something else that would fit as the decoration of his theater's grand sign. When Tuki mentions the Neon Eggs, Boddle states he will accept them in exchange for the Beanstar piece, and then hits Tuki yet again when he claims that the Mario Bros. could never retrieve them.

entities.name: Boddle's Assistant
entities.description:
Boddle's Assistant is a supporting character in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga and its Nintendo 3DS remake Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga + Bowser's Minions.

Boddle's Assistant is a Beanish character with bucked teeth. In the Game Boy version of the game, he has yellow hair and wears a blue shirt. In the 3DS remake, the assistant has his palette changed to have a purple shirt and brown hair and shoes; this is incidentally an unused palette for him in the original Game Boy version.

Boddle's Assistant seems to be pessimistic by the way he spoke to the Bros., believing that they are going to mess up with Boddle. However, Boddle ignored him and aimed to hit him for his impudence. Although he did this action, he seems very loyal to Boddle. He even had no belief that Mario and Luigi will have the ability to get all the Neon Eggs, meaning he is thinking they'll never get them.

entities.name: Bogmire
entities.description:
Bogmire is a shadowy portrait ghost in Luigi's Mansion and its Nintendo 3DS version. He appears as a purple ghost with a large mouth, yellow eyes, and thin, constantly outstretched arms. Bogmire lives under a tombstone in the mansion's Graveyard, and acts as the boss of Area Two. According to his Game Boy Horror entry, Bogmire is the manifestation of the mansion's fear and despair; he does not speak (making him the only area boss without any dialogue), and the Game Boy Horror cannot scan his heart for text. His name is a portmanteau of "bog" and "mire", which refer to different kinds of swampland, likely in reference to his drippy appearance.

At one point, Bogmire was captured by Professor E. Gadd and turned into a portrait; like the other ghosts in the gallery, he was released when King Boo broke in. Bogmire's portrait number in the Gallery is 19; in the GameCube version, he is the only portrait ghost to display another enemy in the portrait, with his gold frame picture depicting a Black Bogmire.

Bogmire can only be fought once Luigi gains access to the Graveyard by vacuuming up Spooky; afterward, a vortex can be accessed via his doghouse, taking Luigi to the Graveyard. Upon clearing the area of the Mr. Bones found there, the large headstone begins to glow. When Luigi approaches it, lightning strikes near the tombstone as Bogmire springs out, and Luigi jumps back in horror. He is then transported into a mysterious arena, where a large Black Bogmire comes out and approaches him, while several others also appear in the field.

Bogmire teleports around the arena, with his presence announced by lightning strikes and the appearance of his shadow; his only means of offense is spawning shadowy translucent doppelgangers called Black Bogmires from the ground (and often from his actual shadow). Bogmire vanishes some time after the Black Bogmires spawn, signaled by his shadow vanishing, and he reappears elsewhere and repeat the pattern. The size of his shadow upon appearing determines the size of the specific Black Bogmire that spawns from it.

Bomb Hammers are rare ghosts that only appear in Luigi's Mansion 3. They are Hammers which are glowing yellow. They can attack by spawning bombs; they also send out a burst of bombs when Luigi or Gooigi slams them to the ground. Bomb Hammers can't be found in The Last Resort, they are only located in the ScareScraper (ten floors mode). They have 350HP.

Bomb Hammers are a form of Hammers, but instead of being red and having white eyes, they are glowing yellow and have blue eyes.

Bomb Hammers won't always appear on the fifth floor of the ScareScraper in the ten floors mod; they appear randomly. To capture them, Luigi has to suck them up in the way he sucks up Hammers. Flash them and stun them first, and suck them from the back. Bomb Hammers will spawn bombs that Luigi has to avoid, be careful when slamming them because the bomb Hammers will send out a burst of bombs when slammed.

entities.name: Bomberman
entities.description:
Bomberman (also specified as White Bomberman or White Bomber) is the titular main protagonist of the series of video games. His first game appearance within any Mario-related media is in the Wario crossover game Wario Blast: Featuring Bomberman!. He also appears alongside Mario and others in three comics published in the German Club Nintendo magazine, as well as in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.

In Wario Blast: Featuring Bomberman!, Wario finds the secret gateway into Bomberland and attempts to plunder its riches and conquer the Madbombers. In the game's campaign, if players choose to play as Bomberman, he fights against Madbombers that look like Wario. If Wario is selected, he fights against Madbombers that look like Bomberman.

Bomberman also appeared as a main character in the comic "Warios Weihnachtsmärchen" (a story based on Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol), published in the German Club Nintendo magazine. In this story, he worked as a sales-clerk in Wario's Bombenladen, a shop selling bombs. When he asked his cold-hearted boss for getting days off during Christmas, Wario fired him, resulting in Bomberman not having enough money to buy Christmas presents for his friends. The Ghosts of Christmas, however, made Wario aware of his bad behavior, so in the end of the story he hired Bomberman again. He serves the same role as Bob Cratchit from the book this story is based around.

Once again, Bomberman played a major role in the comic, "Sag niemals Holerö!". This story is about an evil alien called Heini who is able and plans to turn the humans on Earth into food by singing the magical song, "Holerö". Mario and TicToc, not knowing about the spell yet but noticing its consequences, were among the few who could resist it, and on their way from Switzerland to New York, they met Bomberman in Austria who was not affected by the spell either. Bomberman introduced himself as "Bombi from Vienna", and decided to join Mario and TicToc in order to solve the mystery jointly. The three of them soon met a Toad called Todojewski who told them about Heini and his plans. He also gave the advice to go to "Taj Mahal", a restaurant in Frankfurt, Germany, so Bomberman and his friends went there. In Taj Mahal, they met a man called Mahgo who told each of the heroes about one special power they had. Bomberman's power was throwing bombs.

entities.name: Bombette
entities.description:
Bombette is a character in Paper Mario. She is a Bob-omb who becomes Mario's third partner during his adventure. Like most bombs, Bombette is able to explode, proving useful in breaking holes in cracked walls and floors.

Mario finds her while traversing the Koopa Bros. Fortress. After talking to Mario, she offers to join his party. She demonstrates how to use her skill on a crack in the wall. After the wall has blown up, Bombette realizes that she could have escaped a while ago. Bombette has the ability to body slam enemies as well as using herself as a bomb against a single enemy. Once a Super Block is used on Bombette, she learns how to use Power Bomb, and after another Super Block is used, she will learn Mega Bomb.

entities.name: Bond Ore Salesman
entities.description:
The Bond Ore Salesman is a minor antagonist from Mario & Luigi: Brothership. He can be encountered in a side quest where Dorrie has become sick. The Bond Ore Salesman appears on Desolatt Island.

The Bond Ore Salesman is a tan-skinned Concordian. He wears a brown and green sleeveless top and dark brown trousers whose colour matches the back of his head. His eyes are dark brown, and an antenna sticks up out of the top of his head.

Quite uncharacteristically of most Concordians, who tend to be helpful, the Bond Ore Salesman is a sleazeball, quickly becoming a thorn in the heroes' side by overcharging his wares, and rather cowardly. As a result, the IDLE gang threatens to call more monsters to attack him unless they get the Bond Ore. However, his cowardly nature ultimately results in the gang getting his wares before the salesman runs off anyway.

The Bond Ore Salesman appears in the side quest It's Dorrie!, where Dorrie has become sick, but his injuries can be treated with Bond Ore. Mario and Luigi head over to Desolatt Island to find the Bond Ore. The salesman refuses to part with his wares on the pretense that Princess Peach (who also came to Desolatt for the Bond Ore) is royalty (and therefore too rich to just pay five coins). She refuses, prompting him to try to claim her crown. Mario and Luigi attempt to buy the Bond Ore instead, much to the salesman's ire, only for him to come to the conclusion that they want in on this, which prompts the salesman to push his price up to 99 thousand coins. If the Bros. decline (or if they have too little money), the salesman becomes disappointed by the fact that they are broke as well. However, he gets caught by a Snaptor, which has to be chased after and fought in a miniboss-esque scripted encounter (much to the group's horror). This particular Snaptor is of Level 15 with equal stats to the ones on Lottacoins Island, albeit dropping Desolatt Scraps with a drop rate of 29% rather than Lottacoins Levers, and calls another identical Snaptor to the fight along with two Drillbies.

entities.name: Bonechill
entities.description:
Bonechill is the boss of Chapter 7 in Super Paper Mario.

He is a powerful demon that was released from his prison in the Underwhere by Count Bleck during the events of Super Paper Mario. He is composed of ice and has the power to unleash a freezing wind attack that can freeze Mario or his companions. He also sits upon a giant cannon that can launch large icy bullets.

Rumors persist that Bonechill was once a Nimbi seeing by his wings, his lexicon, and Tippi's tattle of him. However, he is now a skeletal demon that controls the Skellobit army that has been terrorizing the Nimbi. Bonechill and his army of Skellobits invaded The Overthere after his escape in search of the pure heart. Mario and the other heroes were able to defeat him, but not until after his army had frozen most of the residents of The Overthere.

The battle with Bonechill takes place high atop the Nimbi lands of The Overthere, in a chamber where Gram sent Mario at the end of chapter seven. During the battle, Bonechill attacks using his ice breath that cause the target to become frozen, taking four points of damage for a few seconds. While he attacks using his icy breath, the ceiling could get frozen, and thus icicles will begin to fall.

entities.description:
Boneheads is a character in WarioWare, Inc.: Mega Microgame$!. He is a skeleton who bears the appearance of a Japanese shogun.

Boneheads is featured in the plot for Kat & Ana's stage. He possesses the prince or princess of the Diamond City Castle. Ana and a team of six ninjas attempt to stop Boneheads, but all of them fail, so Ana sends a letter to Kat asking for her help. Immediately upon receiving the latter, Kat and her dog, Paw, rush to the Castle, where Boneheads challenges them to come to him on the top floor. The player must clear a series of microgames as Kat and Paw progress along.

At the top, Kat also fails to take out Boneheads, although Paw turns into a sword that Kat uses to rip Boneheads to shreds.

entities.name: Bonetail
entities.description:
Bonetail is found in the Pit of 100 Trials who used to belong to the Shadow Queen, as a pet. The creature was too powerful that she supposedly put her at the very bottom of the Pit of 100 Trials and Bonetail became a mere skeleton following years of being in the Pit of 100 Trials without anything to eat, any of her actions outside of the Pit of 100 Trials, if any, are unknown. Bonetail is the older sister of Gloomtail and Hooktail. She is also known to be the strongest enemy in the game, as her tattle log describes him.

When Mario and co. successfully reach the bottom of the Pit of 100 Trials, they find Bonetail who roars, starting the battle. She has various breath attacks that she uses to attack Mario and co. her blue breath freezes them, her white breath makes them sleepy, green can confuse Mario and co. and finally the purple one can shrink them. When his HP is low, Bonetail can recover her HP by 20 and may stomp on Mario and co. to injure them. Along with that, Bonetail may also chomp them to use as an attack (an un-superguardable attack).

When Mario manages to avoid from fainting along with his allies and defeat her, Bonetail becomes defeated and releases a chest containing the Return Postage badge which makes enemies take half the damage they do to Mario and co.

Bonetail can be very difficult to fight due to the condition Mario may be in from battling the rest of the enemies of the Pit of 100 Trials. First off, Mario should keep a partner that has many HP and the ability to heal oneself without using items. Flurrie is the best choice for this fight (unless Bonetail charges up for her Megabreath attack in which Vivian should be swapped out for her to use her Veil technique). Having the Piercing Blow badge equipped may help as well and having the Feeling Fine badge may help as well. Mario will most likely have more HP at this point so if a partner is feeling weak, then the Quick Change badge should be equipped so that Mario can swap out another partner without wasting his turn. Star Power should be used with Sweet Feast and pulling off Stylish Moves will help as well.

Bonneters can take appearances of other hats and have the ability to capture beings.

entities.name: Bonneter biologist
entities.description:
The Bonneter biologist is a non-playable character in Super Mario Odyssey.

The Bonneter biologist is a scientist. He is eager to expand his knowledge, but is apparently shy, as shown by his habit of not moving from his spot and telling others to bring specimens to him for his research.

The Bonneter biologist appears in the Wooded Kingdom which he is curious how the Uproot stretches. He finds out that Uproots telescope outwards. In the Lost Kingdom, he is curious how Tropical Wigglers stretch their bodies and finds out that it works like an accordion. In Snow Kingdom, he is curious how a Snow Cheep Cheep covers their body in freezing water, and finds out that their round shape and mouth keeps the body insulated. In Bowser's Kingdom, he wants to know how Pokios stretch their beaks. He finds out that they appear to be short due to being in a hyperfolded state that unfolds when the creature's mouth opens.

entities.name: Boo
entities.description:
Boo is one of the five Party Cube hosts in Mario Party 4, alongside Toad, Shy Guy, Koopa Troopa, and Goomba. Boo hosts the board Boo's Haunted Bash.

As shown in the game's end credits, Boo appeared as a generic member of his species before coming across the Party Cube emerging from a Warp Pipe. Together with Toad, Shy Guy, Koopa Troopa and Goomba, they decorated the Party Cube with drawings of themselves before sending an envelope of invitations to Mario and his friends. After dressing up in costumes to match their board themes, they enter the Party Cube and head to find Mario and his friends.

In the game's story mode, Boo, along with the other hosts, promises the player a present should they complete the map. However, after the player beats the map, Boo reveals a catch to the present, claiming the player must beat him in a minigame before they get the present. After defeating him in a game of Mystic Match 'Em, Boo will give the player their present.

According to the Mario Party 4 Prima Guide, Boo is portrayed as a mischievous character, intentionally trying to ruin the party for Mario and his friends by scaring them at any given opportunity. This is strongly shown by his board's theme, which he claims is meant to scare anyone who entered it. Much like the speech of other Boo related characters, Boo constantly gives off mysterious laughter. He also wears a wizard's hat and cape as his costume choice.
