entities.name: Cork and Cask
entities.description:
Cork and Cask are characters in Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga. They are the owners of the Chateau de Chucklehuck.

Cork is the shortest of the brothers and he is wearing a red shirt who resembles Mario. Cask is meant to reference Luigi, as he is taller and wears a green shirt.

They are first seen after Mario and Luigi freed them from a barrel where Popple and Rookie trapped them in. The two duos teach them how to do techniques, Mini-Mario and Luigi Dunk. They request Mario and Luigi to find the Green and Red Goblet, the Mario Bros. then return with the two goblets, pleasing them and allowed them to enter the Chucklehuck Woods.

In Minion Quest: The Search for Bowser, they encounter Captain Goomba and his squad in Reclaim the Red Goblet!. They ask Captain Goomba to reclaim the Red Goblet, which has been stolen from them by a Koopa Paratroopa. When the Red Goblet is returned to them, Cork gives Captain Goomba a map to Mother Chuckalola to help them find Iggy Koopa.

entities.name: Corporal Paraplonk
entities.description:
Corporal Paraplonk is a Koopa Paratroopa with a red shell. He also wears a red bucket on his head. In Mario & Luigi: Dream Team, he now wears a blue bucket with Bowser's symbol on it. He seems to be the strongest of the Elite Trio.

In this game, Corporal Paraplonk is first seen where he notices Bowser wandering around in the woods. Bowser tells Corporal Paraplonk and the others that he is looking for a Banzai Bill to help knock Fawful away from his recently, taken-over castle. Corporal Paraplonk said that one may be deeper in the woods somewhere and Bowser goes out to search. Bowser eventually returns with one and uses Sergeant Guy's cannon to launch the Banzai Bill at Fawful's castle. However, the castle then starts to fly and it crushes Bowser. However, Bowser suddenly grows giant surprising Corporal Paraplonk. During the first giant battle, Corporal Paraplonk teaches the player how to fight as a giant and coaches Bowser throughout the fight telling him when to attack and counterattack. After the battle, Bowser heads into his castle leaving Corporal Paraplonk and the others outside. Corporal Paraplonk and the rest isn't seen again until when Bowser is searching for a Star Cure hidden deep in his castle. They eventually find it but have some delays due to a Fawful Express and Bowser losing his memory. After Bowser opens the safe to get the Star Cure, Corporal Paraplonk, along with Private Goomp and Sergeant Guy, push Bowser into the safe and locks him in. Corporal Paraplonk is excited that they will receive praise from Fawful. However, after Fawful is defeated, Corporal Paraplonk and the others beg for Bowser's forgiveness. Bowser does so by letting them help fix up his castle.

In this game, Corporal Paraplonk and the others have been promoted and they help out in Bowser's conquest of the world along with Antasma. Corporal Paraplonk is then involved in an ambush in the dream world where Mario was fooled by Kamek dressed up as Princess Peach. Corporal Paraplonk, Private Goomp, and Sergeant Guy all fight Mario but they are defeated due to Private Goomp accidentally revealing their weakness. Corporal Paraplonk and the others were then demoted by Kamek to sub down Neo Bowser Castle.

In battle, Corporal Paraplonk attacks with his shell dash, and the target must jump over the shell to avoid damage. If the target lands on the shell, Corporal Paraplonk will be sent into Private Goomp, damaging him, then end up damaging the Goombas in the background.

entities.name: Corrin
entities.description:
Corrin is the customizable avatar character in Fire Emblem Fates. Unlike Robin, however, they are also the main character of the story, having the most prominent role of an avatar character in a Fire Emblem game. The player can select Corrin's gender, physical appearance, voice, stat builds, and secondary class before playing. Corrin is notably half-dragon, being able to transform parts of their body into that of a dragon, or temporarily transform into a dragon with the power of Dragonstones. Corrin and their royal families can use Dragon Vein, a power granted from the ancestral First Dragons, which can be used to alter the user's surrounding terrain in a multitude of ways.

Corrin is a downloadable newcomer in Super Smash Bros. 4 released on February 3, 2016, alongside Bayonetta. Instead of being bundled with a new stage, like with the other DLC newcomers, two new music tracks for Coliseum and Castle Siege will be unlocked alongside Corrin.

Corrin returns alongside the series' entire playable cast in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, this time as an unlockable character. Corrin has a unique victory theme, based upon Lost in Thoughts All Alone, the main theme of Fire Emblem Fates.

Cortez is a skeleton pirate character and a boss in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door. He is the boss of Chapter 5 and is found deep within the Pirate's Grotto on his ship, the Black Skull. He has 20 HP in each of his three forms.

His first form resembles a skeleton with four hands that each carry a weapon: a sword, a rapier, a cutlass, and a hook. Many of his attacks in this form come from his multi-hit sword swings, and the hook, sometimes, poisons the one attacked.

After draining 20 HP from him, he reveals his second form, which looks like a skeletal snake. This is his weakest form, as his attacks deal pretty low damage.

The final form of Cortez is just his head with his three swords and hook floating beside him. This is his strongest form. In this form, he is capable of draining the audience's HP away and adding it to his own.

entities.name: Cosmic Mario
entities.description:
Cosmic Mario is a minor antagonist from the first Super Mario Galaxy. He appears as a boss in Galaxies that have been infected by a Cosmic Comet. As Super Mario Galaxy 2 lacks Cosmic Comets, replacing them with Clone Comets, Cosmic Mario doesn't appear in that game.

Cosmic Mario appears as a Star Bit-filled version of Mario (or Luigi) in Super Mario Galaxy and Super Mario 3D Land. His voice is unusually high-pitched and squeaky. His primary role in the game is similar to Koopa the Quick in Super Mario 64 and Super Mario 64 DS, and Il Piantissimo from Super Mario Sunshine, in which the player races him to get an award; in this case, a Power Star/Flag Pole. Holding Z when in the ready position causes Mario or Luigi to get a boost. The races are slightly more difficult against Cosmic Luigi.

Cosmic Mario resembles Shadow Mario's appearance and Cosmic Clones. It was given to him to add a space effect to the character.

Cosmic Mario/Luigi is only in a galaxy if there is a Cosmic Comet orbiting the galaxy. Cosmic Comets appear in the following galaxies:

entities.name: Cosmic Spirit
entities.description:
Cosmic Spirit is a character in Super Mario Galaxy 2 with a female human shape just like that of Rosalina.

When Mario talks to her, Cosmic Spirit will ask if he needs to be shown the way to any Stars. If the player agrees to do so, the Cosmic Spirit will transform into a blue orb that will encircle and gain control of Mario. This blue orb will guide Mario to the Power Star, but will not collect any Star Bits, coins, comet medals, or 1-ups and health mushrooms, all on purpose. This downside is most obviously demonstrated on the level Tall Trunk's Big Slide. While there is the option of regaining control of Mario by use of the + button, doing so is virtual suicide as this will make the Power Star degrade to a Bronze Star, in which you have to replay the level to get the Power Star. She was formerly voiced by Rosalina's very first former voice actress Mercedes Rose.

Note that while the Cosmic Spirit assists the player, Cosmic Mario and Cosmic Luigi antagonize players instead of helping them. The cosmic spirit also turns out to be Rosalina.

entities.name: Count Bleck
entities.description:
Count Bleck, also known by his real name, Lord Blumiere, is an evil count and the central antagonist of Super Paper Mario. During the game, he summons the Chaos Heart by forcefully marrying Princess Peach to Bowser and uses it to open The Void, which has the power to destroy all dimensions. He also leads a troop of minions, with its primary members being Nastasia, O'Chunks, Mimi, Mr. L, and Dimentio.

His name, "Bleck", is normally used as onomatopoeia for disgust, but can also be interpreted as a corruption of "Black", referring to darkness (his Japanese name is a play on the French word for "black", noir.) His real name is likely a portmanteau of blue, referring to his color, and lumière, the French term for light and a reference to his status as a member of the Tribe of Darkness.

Count Bleck wears a white top hat and coat, and is usually shrouded in a cape with a gradient of white at its top fading to blue at the bottom. The inside of the cape is dark blue and starry, and when he opens his cape during the cutscene in Bowser's Castle, a unique design is shown. This design is from Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door, and depicts the pattern used atop the pedestal in the room with The Thousand-Year Door when Mario presents a Crystal Star. He also wears a large red brooch, white gloves, and wields a brown scepter topped with a blue jewel. On his left eye is a monocle, and his eyes and mouth are both red and glowing. However, both his eyes and mouth become light blue when he is defeated, and remains like that until the Pure Hearts are restored.

Count Bleck's motives in the game are mostly caused by the sadness of losing Timpani. At the start of the game, he seems to be a villain with no feelings who wishes to end all worlds due to the power given by Dark Prognosticus. As the story progresses, his sympathetic traits are revealed and reasons are given to his actions.

entities.name: Count Cannoli
entities.description:
Count Cannoli is one of the two secondary antagonists of Wario: Master of Disguise. He is a who stars in The Silver Zephyr, a TV show that Wario watches. He uses his wand, Goodstyle, to transform into the show's title character, the Silver Zephyr. This inspires Wario to jump into the show himself and steal Goodstyle. As a result of this, as well as their mutual desire to obtain the pieces of the Wishstone, Wario and Cannoli develop a bitter rivalry. Count Cannoli's name comes from the , an Italian dessert. Similar to Mario, he has an Italian accent and shouts "Mamamia" when defeated in his second and third boss fights.

Count Cannoli is first seen while Wario is watching The Silver Zephyr on his television. Preparing to rob the S.S. Caviar, he uses Goodstyle turn into the eponymous thief, prompting Wario to invent the Telmet and steal Goodstyle. Infuriated, Cannoli pursues Wario throughout the ship and booby traps it, but he is unable to get Goodstyle back. He confronts Wario at the top of the ship and attacks him with his battle machine, Mad Hat Mk. I. However, Wario destroys it, and Cannoli instead decides to strike a deal with Wario. In exchange for returning Goodstyle, Cannoli was going to assist Wario in finding and stealing treasure. Though Wario agrees, Cannoli immediately calls off the deal when Goodstyle reveals that a piece of the Wishstone is on the ship. Cannoli prepares another battle machine, Mad Hat Mk. II, to face Wario in the cargo bay where the tablet is, but he is once again unable to defeat Wario. Cannoli disappears, and Wario takes the Wishstone piece.

Cannoli follows Wario to the Smithsnorian Museum and overhears him speaking with the Sphinx about a cave hidden by a perpetual blizzard. Knowing that they are referring to Sneezemore Cave, Cannoli gets there first and spies on Wario while hiding inside a snowman. After Wario meets Carpaccio and has his progress halted by four stone doors, Cannoli demands Goodstyle back in exchange for telling him how to open the doors. Wario refuses and finds the four bird-shaped crystals needed to open the doors without Cannoli's help, then shuts them again to prevent Cannoli from following him.

Count Down appears to be controlled by the Ding-A-Lings, and all of them work for Smithy of his gang. Count Down and the Ding-A-Lings are also fought in The Factory.

Count Down is a very unique boss at it uses magical attacks depending on what the time the clock hands land on.

The key to defeating Count Down is to defeat the two Ding-A-Lings on its head so that they will not all attack at once. Count Down is also weak to Jump attacks, thunder attacks, and Snowy so Mario and Mallow are highly recommended for this fight.

entities.name: Count Fang
entities.description:
Count Fang is the leader of the Fangs and a boss in Yoshi's New Island. Count Fang was originally a normal-sized Fang before being enlarged by Kamek. Count Fang is the boss of World 2 and the game’s second major boss. Defeating Count Fang will unlock World 3.

After the Blue Yoshi and Baby Mario survive Count Fang's Castle, they come face to face with Count Fang himself, Kamek then emerges to taunt Yoshi before using his Magic Hammer to enlarge Count Fang making him massive.

Count Fang begins the battle by flying to the ceiling of the chamber and roosting (when he does this he is immune to any attacks), this move calls several Purple Fangs who fly to their master, Count Fang then descends and his Purple Fang underlings will fly circling him as Count Fang flies towards Yoshi, Yoshi should aim an egg so it flies by the Purple Fangs and hits the Count himself, if it hits a Purple Fang, it will be eliminated leaving Count Fang open (the Purple Fangs can also be swallowed for eggs if Yoshi is running low), if Yoshi waits too long, Count Fang will roost again and call more Purple Fangs, upon being hit, Count Fang will descend to the ground and spin trying to ram into Yoshi, Yoshi should avoid this as being hit will cost him some Stars which will prevent a 100 Point score. After Count Fang is done with his spin attack, he will roost again and call more Purple Fangs, Count Fang will descend again with his minions, Yoshi should avoid them and hit Count Fang again, he will repeat the same process only faster this time before roosting again and calling even more Purple Fangs, hit Count Fang once more to finish him off.

entities.name: Coursebot
entities.description:
Coursebot is the robot companion of the player in Super Mario Maker, Super Mario Maker for Nintendo 3DS and Super Mario Maker 2. It allows the player to save their levels and download levels from other players.

Coursebot allows the player to save and download levels in the Super Mario Maker games. His icon resembles the robot in Mario Paint when a picture is being saved to the console.

In both Super Mario Maker and Super Mario Maker for Nintendo 3DS, Coursebot only appears when the player is saving a level, downloading a level or loading a level. It is introduced to the player in the tutorial when first starting the game.

Coursebot acts the same as before. He also appears in the Story mode as a bonus for completing the game, and Coursebot is used to replay cutscenes from earlier after the player frees him from being stuck in the ground.

entities.name: Cow
entities.description:
Cow is a character appearing in Mario Kart World.

Cow is a cute, white bovine creature that resembles the Moo Moo, down to having beady eyes and her body having a few black spots, with one around her right eye. Her nose has a ring run through it, and she wears a blue collar that has a bell hung from it. In the character select screen, Cow walks on all fours, but gameplay shows that she is still capable of driving and presumably walking upright.

Cow was revealed in the Nintendo Direct for Mario Kart World on [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3pE23YTYEZM April 2, 2025], and is shown after Mario drives his own car on a wall in a similar style to Anti-gravity. She can be seen riding a bike on a power line. Cow's emblem consists of a stylised depiction of a Moo Moo's face.

Cow was unlockable in version 1.0.0, but she was made available following a software update. She is a heavyweight driver.

entities.description:
Cowboy Jed is a live-action Mario character who appears in the American commercials for Mario Kart Wii, the only few times that he made an appearance. He has a son named Jed Junior, who sometimes appears alongside him.

Cowboy Jed is a parody of a car dealership owner, and instead owns a "kart dealership" titled Mario Kart Emporium, which he invites the viewer to visit. However, the location is neither seen nor is it the focus of the commercials, as after Cowboy Jed mentions the Mario Kart Emporium, he moves on to promoting Mario Kart Wii itself.

The Canadian French version of the Mario Kart Wii commercials feature a different actor for Cowboy Jed.

entities.name: Cozette
entities.description:
Cozette, also called Ms. Cozette by her pupil Connie, is the overarching protagonist of Mario & Luigi: Brothership who serves as an ally to Mario and Luigi. Cozette was the original Wattanist (a pun on "botanist"), or caretaker, of the Uni-Tree before she disappeared, forcing Connie to supplant her.

Cozette is a relatively tall, slim Concordian woman. As with her student Connie, her face resembles an outlet. Her outfit consists of a hat that resembles a plug and a blue dress with a black scarf. On the dress's back is a symbol to the symbol that Zokket has on the back of his cape. Cozette has similar proportions to certain taller Concordians like Dulles, Technikki, and Prince Chilliam.

Cozette is described as a pro Wattanist. She cares for Concordia and the Concordians, and hopes that Connie can succeed her as a Wattanist successfully. After his death, she blames herself for what Zokket did, which can imply that she is partly responsible for it.

Cozette is mentioned several times by her student Connie throughout the game, and it is revealed that she helped Connie through trouble. When Zokket confronts the latter aboard Shipshape Island, taunting her how his Glohm wave killed Mario and Luigi as the two left the Zokket Fortress, Connie refuses to give up hope, proclaiming that she believes her mentor will come someday.

Cractus is a character in the Wario franchise. It first appears in Wario Land 4.

Cractus is a large, drooling with leaf-like appendages.

Cractus first appears as a boss in Wario Land 4 and is one of the four non-first/final bosses of the game in which the Player(s) can fight in any order. It is the guardian of the Emerald Passage.

Upon starting the battle, Cractus is sleeping, ignoring Wario's presence. To force it to battle, Wario must simply ram the vase holding it. This will cause Cractus to wake up. In normal mode, the time limit of the battle is 4:00; in Hard mode it is 3:00; and in S-Hard mode, it is 2:00.

entities.description:
Cranberry is only mentioned during Luigi's adventures and is known to being one of the last of the Luffs. In the Rapturous Ruins, Luigi found the sleeping Cranberry who then woke the Luff up by calling out to him. Luigi then earned the ability to speak Cranberry's language and Cranberry explains to him that the Luffs were once a great empire due to their usage of the Marvelous Compass. However, they soon became drunk with power and Cranberry had no choice but to split the Marvelous Compass into seven different parts and hide them throughout the Waffle Kingdom. Cranberry then went into a thousand-year sleep until a hero who was collecting the Marvelous Compass pieces came. Luigi is revealed to be this hero and Cranberry gives him the last of the Marvelous Compass pieces. With his purpose now fulfilled, Luff fades away hoping Luigi can rescue Princess Eclair.

entities.description:
Craw-Daddy, also known as The Dark Gatekeeper, is a Dark Craw and fighter in Glitzville found in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door. His name is a play on both his species and "crawdad," a name sometimes used for the . He is ranked fourth in the Glitz Pit, below Hamma, Bamma, and Flare but above The Fuzz. Once Mario wins the championship, he is moved into fifth.

Since Craw-Daddy uses his spear to attack, Mario is not able to jump on him without getting hurt unless he has Spike Shield. Instead, Mario must rely heavily on hammer attacks or using items. Although he has no defense, he makes up for it with a high amount of health and powerful attacks.

Like all Dark Craws, he has red eyes and dark-blue skin, as well as a brown vest and bandana and a red handkerchief, compared to the green and tan clothing that regular Craws wear.

entities.description:
Crazy Hand (クレイジーハンド Kureijī Hando) is a villain in the Super Smash Bros. series, first appearing in the game Super Smash Bros. Melee. Like his right-handed counterpart, Master Hand, he is a large, disembodied, gloved hand, though he is a left hand instead of a right hand.

Unlike Master Hand, who embodies a creation, Crazy Hand embodies a being of destruction. Crazy Hand is voiced by Dean Harrington (Melee), Pat Cashman (Brawl), and Xander Mobus (3DS / Wii U, Ultimate), who also voiced the announcer of the respective games.

Crazy Hand is a more dangerous foe than Master Hand, since he has more attacks, and many of his attacks also have side effects, such as the Lip's Stick flower. Crazy Hand also attacks more frequently, giving fewer opportunities to hit, which makes the battle in Classic Mode harder because the fight with him and Master Hand is timed.

entities.name: The Creepy Steeple Boo
entities.description:
The Creepy Steeple Boo is a character who appears in Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door. He resides at the Creepy Steeple for the remainder of the game.

The Creepy Steeple Boo is first seen during Chapter 4 after Mario has opened a treasure chest that contained many Boos in it. The Creepy Steeple Boo then asks Mario a question on how many Boos were in the chest. If Mario guesses correctly (which is 200), The Creepy Steeple Boo gives Mario an Ultra Shroom which is a very rare item to obtain in the game. Later in the game, The Creepy Steeple Boo then sends Mario an email thanking him for freeing him and his friends earlier. He then tells Mario that there are treasures that might be still in the Creepy Steeple if he were to visit again (most likely referring to the secret room near the entrance that contains the Cookbook and a Shine Sprite further reinforced that The Creepy Steeple Boo took the picture near the entrance for the tube mode).

entities.name: Crime Wave Clyde
entities.description:
Crime Wave Clyde is a character who only appears in the The Adventures of Super Mario Bros. 3 episode "Crimes R Us."

Crime Wave Clyde is from Earth, where he had been sentenced to 12,423 years with no parole due to his extensive criminal record.

Crime Wave Clyde plays a major role in "Crimes R Us." Here, King Koopa and his Koopalings travel to Clyde's prison on the Doom Ship, where he is taken to by Bully Koopa. Following King Koopa's request, Clyde agrees to teach the Koopalings everything that he knows about crime to help them become expert criminals. King Koopa, crossing his fingers behind his back, tells Clyde that he can keep half of whatever they steal.

The first lesson Clyde gives to the Koopalings is bank robbery. After receiving a crash course from Clyde, the Koopalings raid the First Mushroom Bank, but are foiled by Mario and Luigi in the process.

entities.name: 502 Bathroom
entities.description:
502 Bathroom is a room in Luigi's Mansion 3.

502 Bathroom is found in the RIP Suites, the fifth floor of The Last Resort. It is a bathroom entered from Mario's hotel room, Room 502. The 502 Bathroom has the usual bathroom features, including a bathtub, a sink, and a toilet. In addition, there is a drain in the floor.

The 502 Bathroom's entrance is initially blocked by a cart is blocking the door, preventing Luigi from exploring the bathroom. The next time he explores the RIP Suites, Luigi can use the Suction Shot on the cart to clear the door and explore the 502 Bathroom.

Gooigi can fall through the drain in the floor. In the area below the drain, Gooigi can use a Suction Shot to pull off the wood barring the valve, then turn the valve all the way so that the flowing water is redirected to the bathtub, unblocking the path to the treasure chest.

entities.name: ? Island
entities.description:
? Island is one of the eleven islands of The Great Sea in Paper Mario: The Origami King. It is located in the B-5 Tile on the Sea Chart. The island consists of Origami Stone Spikes, Origami Sidesteppers, many Question Blocks, and a Paper Macho Stone Spike on top of the hill. A Sensor Lab can be located here.

The island as the name says it is shaped like a question mark. It is a grassy island with slopes where the Origami Stone Spikes throws rocks. In the center area are a floor made out of Question Blocks where the Sidestepers are located. entities.name: Africa
entities.description:
Africa is a real-world continent found on Earth. Its first appearance in Mario-related media is the Saturday Supercade episode "Hairy Parent," but the first appearance of Africa in a Mario game is Mario is Missing!. Egypt is the most famous country within Africa and the most recurring within Mario-related media.

In Mario is Missing!, Luigi visits a few cities in Africa on his journey to rescue Mario, including:

In all versions of Mario's Time Machine, Egypt is featured as one of the locations that Mario travels to.

While not appearing in gameplay, Africa, along with Earth's other continents, is featured on the online racing menus in the entries of the Mario Kart series that support online play, including Mario Kart DS, Mario Kart Wii, Mario Kart 7, and Mario Kart 8 along with its remake Mario Kart 8 Deluxe.
